title: Report command parsing
responsibility: Parses report command options and reads required values or JSON input.

inputs.name: reportCli.argv
inputs.description: The first argument is the operation; remaining arguments are parsed as flags and positionals. Parsing is permissive, allows positionals, and recognizes the declared string and boolean options.

inputs.name: inputData.flags
inputs.description: Flags supplying JSON through `file` or `data`; a truthy `file` is read as UTF-8 and takes precedence over `data`. If the selected content is falsy, the function throws.

inputs.name: required.flags
inputs.description: Flags to inspect at the supplied name. The selected value must be a nonblank string; whitespace is checked with `trim()` but preserved in the returned value.

inputs.name: required.name
inputs.description: The key in `flags` whose value is required to be a nonblank string. The function uses this name in the missing-value error message with a `--` prefix.

outputs.name: reportCli
outputs.description: An object containing the first argument as `operation` (or an empty string), parsed option values as `flags`, and remaining positional arguments. The parser permits unknown options and positionals, with declared string and boolean options.

outputs.name: inputData
outputs.description: Resolves to the JSON value parsed from the truthy `file` contents or, when no truthy file is supplied, from `data`. The value is cast to a record without runtime shape validation.

outputs.name: required
outputs.description: The original string at `flags[name]` when it is nonblank. Surrounding whitespace is retained.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: `inputData` throws this when neither selected JSON source is truthy, and `required` throws it when the selected value is not a nonblank string. File-read errors propagate unchanged.

errors.name: SyntaxError
errors.description: Propagates from `JSON.parse` when the selected file contents or inline data are not valid JSON.

errors.name: TypeError
errors.description: Propagates from `parseArgs` when an argument violates the declared option type, such as supplying a value to a boolean option.
